sources.entry: FHEM - Automate common tasks in the household like switching lamps and heating. It can also be used to log events like temperature or power consumption. You can control it via web or smartphone frontends, telnet or TCP/IP directly. (Source Code) GPL-3.0 Perl

summary.name: FHEM
summary.one_liner: FHEM is a GPL-licensed Perl server for house automation that controls lamps, shutters and heating and logs sensor data such as temperature, humidity and power consumption.
use_cases: control heating from a web or smartphone interface
log temperature, humidity or power consumption
connect Z-Wave, KNX or EnOcean devices to one server
send events to external scripts or programs
run timed commands such as lights on from sunset to midnight
summary.what_it_does: FHEM runs as a 24/7 Perl server that connects to attached hardware such as USB sticks (CUL, EnOcean, Z-Wave) to reach actors and sensors. It supports a large set of protocols and devices, including KNX, Z-Wave, EnOcean, Philips Hue, HomeMatic, MQTT, HomeKit and various TVs, speakers and amplifiers. It can automatically create devices and log files when new sensor data arrives, and logs events to files or a database with regex filters. Users can control it through a built-in web frontend, third-party smartphone and tablet frontends, telnet or TCP/IP interfaces, and it can notify external programs on certain events. The page cites over 430 modules.
notable: Automatically creates devices and plots when new sensor data arrives
Over 430 modules covering many protocols and device brands
Multiple interfaces: plain text, JSON, XML over TCP/IP, SSL or HTTP
Available as tar.gz, zip, deb, and Docker container image
caveats: Requires a 24/7 server with Perl and usually attached USB hardware
The page advises against running it on Fritz!Box because AVM removed the ability to auto-start foreign programs after reboot
